newsitem.title: GERMANY: BOJ - credit policy not direct cause for weak yen.
newsitem.headline: BOJ - credit policy not direct cause for weak yen.

text.p: Bank of Japan Governor Yasuo Matsushita said on Saturday that Japan's easy credit policy was not a direct cause of the recent weakening of the yen.

Matsushita told a briefing after a meeting of Group of Seven (G7) finance leaders and central bank chiefs that the Japanese central bank's monetary policy has been in place since 1995 and was geared to ensure sustainable growth.
"You cannot link this easy monetary policy, which has been in place over the last two years, for the recent weakening of the yen," Matsushita said after the Berlin meeting had ended.
Japan's monetary policy takes a lot of factors into consideration, not just currency market developments, he said.
